project.name: GnuTLS
project.commit_note: The exact staged vulnerable source inspected for Stage 02 is the ARVO workspace checkout at `90a71b2e53e9696bd4c07ff98a12d06ecd2e424d`, whose line map matches the statements cited below. Sample metadata separately records `c7cbef52c27217c3bd529ddef26152fb11093a12` / `d165c2a37f7d072cc88db88ec97f057a9ac6e4aa`, but the staged `patch.diff` only changes `lib/includes/gnutls/gnutls.h.in` comments and does not touch the crashing DN-parser path in `lib/x509/common.c`.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42470155 (gnutls): Use-of-uninitialized-value found by fuzz target gnutls_dn_parser_fuzzer [msan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42470155
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged 13-byte witness `30 0b 31 09 30 07 06 03 55 04 07 1f 16` is imported by `gnutls_x509_dn_import` as an X.509 Name and later re-exported through `gnutls_x509_dn_get_str`. While walking the first AttributeTypeAndValue, `append_elements` reads OID `2.5.4.7` from bytes `06 03 55 04 07` and the raw attribute value bytes `1f16`, so `_gnutls_x509_dn_to_string` routes that value through `decode_complex_string`'s complex `DirectoryString` path. `decode_complex_string` declares fixed stack buffer `char str[MAX_STRING_LEN]` without initialization and then calls `asn1_read_value(tmpasn, "", str, &len)` to read the CHOICE label. The staged build script compiles and installs external `libtasn1` from `_work/src/libtasn1` before configuring GnuTLS, and that library's CHOICE read path (`lib/element.c:659-667, 994-996`) copies only `_asn1_strlen(node->down->name) + 1` bytes into the caller buffer. Because `decode_complex_string` never clears `str` and never uses `len` to bound the subsequent keyword dispatch, `strcmp(str, "teletexString")` reads into the uninitialized tail of `str`; the saved MemorySanitizer trace reports the first poisoned byte at offset 11 inside the 14-byte comparison window and attributes the origin to `str`'s stack allocation in `decode_complex_string`. The staged `patch.diff` is unrelated and does not resolve this path.

source.description: First project-code statement that consumes the attacker-controlled witness bytes and materializes them into the ASN.1 Name object later traversed by the crashing exporter.
source.value_from: The fuzz harness passes the exact staged `poc` blob `30 0b 31 09 30 07 06 03 55 04 07 1f 16` as `raw.data/raw.size` into `gnutls_x509_dn_import(dn, &raw)`, and this decode stores those bytes into `dn->asn` for later DN-string export.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant uninitialized bytes originate in stack buffer `str`. MemorySanitizer identifies this allocation in `decode_complex_string` as the source of the poisoned data later consumed by `strcmp`.
tainted_value_origin.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports the allocation context at line 347, which is the function-entry line in this snapshot; the actual `str` declaration is line 348.

sink.description: MSAN crash site. The first fixed-keyword dispatch compares `str` against the 13-character literal `teletexString` plus its NUL terminator, reading a 14-byte window from `str` that still contains uninitialized tail bytes.
sink.note: The staged `sanitizer_trace.txt` reports `Uninitialized bytes in __interceptor_memcmp at offset 11 inside [str, 14)` and then `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at `lib/x509/common.c:390:6` in `decode_complex_string`.

root_cause.description: Partial initialization root cause. `decode_complex_string` asks libtasn1 to store the CHOICE name in fixed stack buffer `str`, but the library writes only the CHOICE-name prefix plus one NUL byte, leaving the remainder of `str` unchanged even though later code treats the buffer as fully initialized for keyword comparisons.
root_cause.note: In the staged run, `_work/src/build.sh:23-26,45` builds and links external `_work/src/libtasn1`. Its `PUT_STR_VALUE` macro (`lib/element.c:659-667`) sets `*len = _asn1_strlen(data) + 1` and copies only that many bytes, and the CHOICE arm at `lib/element.c:994-996` uses that macro for `asn1_read_value(tmpasn, "", str, &len)`. `decode_complex_string` never zeroes `str` and never checks `len` before the `strcmp` chain, so the later compare reads the untouched tail. The staged `patch.diff` and metadata `fixed_commit` are unrelated to this obligation.

parser_admitted.description: The exact witness is admitted into the target parser because `_asn1_strict_der_decode` succeeds here, so this error branch is not taken and `gnutls_x509_dn_import` returns 0.
parser_admitted.condition: On the saved Stage 01 run, `result == ASN1_SUCCESS`, allowing `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` to proceed to `gnutls_x509_dn_get_str(dn, &out)` and the crashing DN export path.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness wraps the exact 13-byte witness in `gnutls_datum_t raw`, imports it as a DN, and then asks GnuTLS to stringify that DN.
GnuTLS decodes the attacker-controlled DER bytes into `dn->asn`, preserving the witness Name structure for later export.
DN export walks the first AttributeTypeAndValue, reads OID `2.5.4.7` and raw value bytes `1f16`, and routes that known OID through `_gnutls_x509_dn_to_string`'s complex-string decoder.

The complex-string decoder stores a short CHOICE name into uninitialized fixed stack buffer `str` and immediately dispatches on `strcmp`; the first `teletexString` comparison reads past the initialized prefix and triggers the saved MemorySanitizer report.

fine_trace.note: Source. GnuTLS decodes the exact attacker-controlled witness bytes into `dn->asn`, materializing the ASN.1 Name object later traversed by DN string export.
While exporting the imported Name, `append_elements` reads the first AVA's OID string into `oid`. For the exact witness bytes `06 03 55 04 07`, this becomes `2.5.4.7`.
The same AVA's raw DER value bytes are materialized into `tvd`. For the witness, `tvd.data/tvd.size` carries the two-byte attribute value `1f16`.

fine_trace.code: if (oentry->asn_desc != NULL) { /* complex */ ret = decode_complex_string(oentry, value, value_size, &tmp); }
fine_trace.note: Known OID `2.5.4.7` resolves to an entry with non-NULL `asn_desc`, so GnuTLS treats `tvd` as a complex `DirectoryString` and enters `decode_complex_string` instead of the unknown-OID hex fallback.
MSAN origin. `decode_complex_string` allocates fixed stack buffer `str` without initialization, so every byte is indeterminate until a later write defines it.

The raw attribute value bytes from step 3 are decoded into temporary ASN.1 object `tmpasn`. This succeeds on the witnessed path; otherwise `_gnutls_x509_dn_to_string` would fall back to hex output and the later `strcmp` sink would not execute.

Root cause. `decode_complex_string` asks libtasn1 for the CHOICE name in fixed buffer `str`. In the staged build, external `_work/src/libtasn1/lib/element.c` handles CHOICE reads by `PUT_STR_VALUE`, which copies only `_asn1_strlen(node->down->name) + 1` bytes into the caller buffer. Because `str` came from step 5 uninitialized, bytes beyond that copied prefix remain poisoned. The saved MSan report's first poisoned byte at offset 11 inside `[str, 14)` shows the later `teletexString` compare read past this initialized prefix.
This writes a terminator at the end of the copied CHOICE-name prefix but does not define the remainder of `str`. The code still does not use `len` to bound the keyword dispatch that follows.

Sink. The first dispatch compares `str` against 13-character literal `teletexString` plus NUL, so the compare reads a 14-byte window from `str`. Steps 7-8 initialized only the copied prefix and its terminator, leaving the tail poisoned; the saved trace reports `Uninitialized bytes in __interceptor_memcmp at offset 11 inside [str, 14)` and then `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at this line.

allocation_context.note: The saved trace says the uninitialized value was created by allocation of `str` in the stack frame of `decode_complex_string`; the exact `char str[MAX_STRING_LEN], tmpname[128];` declaration is line 348 in the staged checkout.

sanitizer_ground_truth.crash_summary: MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value in decode_complex_string; stack decode_complex_string -> _gnutls_x509_dn_to_string -> append_elements matches OSS-Fuzz issue 42470155.
sanitizer_ground_truth.source: parsed from Stage 01 sanitizer_trace.txt and reproduction_report.json

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: MemorySanitizer names `str`'s stack allocation in `decode_complex_string` as the origin, and the fine trace closes why those stack bytes remain poisoned: external libtasn1 copies only the CHOICE-name prefix into fixed buffer `str` before the `strcmp` sink reads past it.
cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged `patch.diff` and metadata `fixed_commit` only modify `lib/includes/gnutls/gnutls.h.in` documentation comments and do not touch `lib/x509/common.c`, `lib/x509/dn.c`, or `lib/x509/x509_dn.c`, so the staged patch does not resolve the reproduced DN-parser crash.

format.name: Raw DER X.509 Name blob consumed by gnutls_dn_parser_fuzzer
format.contract: The verified trigger is exactly the staged 13-byte blob `30 0b 31 09 30 07 06 03 55 04 07 1f 16`. On the saved run, `gnutls_x509_dn_import` accepts it as a Name with one AttributeTypeAndValue whose type bytes encode OID `2.5.4.7`, and later DN export feeds the raw value bytes `1f16` into `decode_complex_string`. There, external libtasn1 copies only a short CHOICE-name prefix into fixed stack buffer `str`, and the first keyword comparison `strcmp(str, "teletexString")` reads the uninitialized tail of that buffer. The staged artifacts do not establish a broader class of malformed DirectoryString encodings, so the contract should not be generalized beyond this exact witness.
